# dsh-speed
Fast and Ultrafast for DSH web, terminal commands, and agent model requests. Managed source: nix-con
for DSH web, terminal commands, and agent model requests. Managed source: nix-config/pkgs/dsh-speed.
## Use
Open the existing **Model / Effort** menu and choose **Speed**: Standard, Fast, or Ultrafast. In `ds
t`, `/speed` opens an arrow-key picker when all three speeds are available; use Up/Down and Enter, o
r Escape to cancel. With only Standard and Fast available it toggles between them. `/speed status` r
eports the current choice, and `/speed standard`, `/speed fast`, `/speed ultrafast` set it directly.
The start screen and bottom bar display `Speed: Standard`, `Speed: ⚡` (Fast), or `Speed: ⚡⚡` (Ultra
fast). Changes apply to subsequent requests. A web selection during streaming leaves the active requ
est unchanged; the terminal command requires an idle agent.
Selections are independent for each session, provider, and model. Titles and other auxiliary request
s do not inherit the conversational speed. Teammates start with their own Standard selection; their
authentication still uses the same configured provider. A parent's Fast or Ultrafast setting never s
ilently spills into a teammate.
| Route | Credential source | Speed availability |

| Local `openai-codex` | Local Codex `auth.json` | That account's native model catalog |
| Configure

d `providerproxy` | ProviderProxy client key | Proxy `/v1/models` catalog |
| Official `openai` API
| Existing DSH API credential | Explicit supported-model list / configured opt-ins |
**Fast sends `priority`; Ultrafast sends `ultrafast`.** Native requests also send Codex's `x-codex-r
outing-hint`. Standard sends `default` after explicitly selecting it. Before selection the existing
transport defaults apply.
## Authentication and configuration
Managed profiles read `~/.codex/auth.json` directly for local Codex requests, including agents. They
do not copy refresh tokens into DSH's credential store. Reads follow the current file so an account
switch takes effect on the next request. Near expiry, the configured Codex executable refreshes its
own login through `account/read`; DSH then rereads the file. Missing or invalid native credentials
fail visibly. Use `codex login` if that device has never signed in.
ProviderProxy is a separate credential plane. The launcher reads its client key from the managed tok
en file; the proxy owns and refreshes its upstream OAuth login. Local Codex tokens are never forward
ed to the proxy. Only an explicitly configured provider with the exact allowed base URL can receive
proxy speed options.

Use the managed Nix profile to upgrade; do not install a duplicate row. DSH must restart to load a n
ew host plugin. The Model/Effort child slot is a checked build-time patch to pinned DSH 0.2.1-alpha.
2. Runtime transport compatibility is audited for pi-ai 0.87.1 and 1.1.0; other versions fail rather
than silently ignoring speed.
The native catalog caches for five minutes and the proxy catalog for one minute, keyed by credential
s. Refresh forces a new catalog read. Unknown models, unavailable credentials, and failed catalogs e
xpose only Standard. A revoked saved tier warns and rejects generation until a valid speed is select
se only Standard. A revoked saved tier warns and rejects generation until a valid speed is selected.
Preferences default to `~/.dsh/dsh-speed.json.d/`, one atomically replaced 0600 record per session/p
rovider/model in a 0700 directory. Independent web and terminal processes cannot overwrite unrelated
records. Existing array-format `dsh-speed.json` is a read-only migration fallback. `stateFile: fals
e` uses memory only.

## Tests
The Nix derivation runs unit, property, client, runtime, and pinned-bundle contract tests. The real
DSH E2E suite uses an isolated HOME, workspace, port, and tmux socket with synthetic HTTP credential
s. It exercises native and proxy routes, six model/tier combinations, browser persistence and isolat
ion, busy states, narrow layout, terminal commands, and Team delegation.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
All real-account tests are gated. `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` use only synthetic credentials a
nd loopback HTTP mocks. Direct live-runner invocation refuses before reading credentials unless `--l
ive` or `DSH_LIVE_TESTS=1` is supplied. Real agent E2E additionally requires `DSH_LIVE_AGENTS=1`; ru
n it only deliberately with `npm run test:live:agents`.
Real-account smoke tests consume plan allowance. From the nix-config root:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Native tests use the actual local auth bridge with an empty DSH credential store. Proxy tests use th
e same managed token file as the launcher. They save selections through the public handler, inspect
the final HTTP payload, require a successful terminal response and `SPEED_OK`, and report requested
and returned tiers separately. Unsupported account tiers are reported explicitly. Timing is diagnost
ic, not a benchmark.
## Native protocol evidence
**Native comparison, 2026-10-10, bundled Codex CLI 0.160.1:** isolated real CLI runs using the same
local OAuth login completed all six model/mode combinations with `SPEED_OK`. A loopback proxy scoped
only to those CLI processes captured the actual WebSocket requests to `wss://chatgpt.com/backend-ap
i/codex/responses`; the running desktop app and system trust store were unchanged. The native wire c
onses`; the running desktop app and system trust store were unchanged. The native wire contract was:
| Mode | `response.create.service_tier` | `x-codex-routing-hint` on the WebSocket handshake |

| Standard | omitted | `model=<model>` |
| Fast | `priority` | `model=<model>;tier=priority` |
| Ult
rafast | `ultrafast` | `model=<model>;tier=ultrafast` |
